title: openai-wire-is-a-machine-anybody-can-include
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/machines/openai_wire owns the wire format and nothing else
intention: cairn/machines/openai_wire is a machine any holder can include: it speaks the OpenAI chat-completions wire format on one side and calls an INJECTED resolve callable on the other. A shim that fronts an OpenAI-shaped foreign process includes it, hands it a resolve that asks inference_domain over the bus, and the process gets a door it already knows how to speak — without the wire format ever entering a device, and without the process ever dialling a provider itself.
why: Akien's ruling, 2026-09-11, verbatim: 'the shims handle all the interfacing with the outside world. it's what allows us to integrate a device. adding a port on the inference proxy, as sensible as that is, and it really is, the architecture wants to force everything to be similar specifically because fewer things to know as you or i switch between pieces. extra work to make it all the same to be sure. but all the same means less cogniting on which path is right.' And then the rung, also his: 'and if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it.' Law 6 is what is being bought — a foreign process that dials a provider directly IS a second door to the inference host, and the only way to close it is to offer a door it already knows how to speak. Law 1 is what is being banked: the next OpenAI-shaped process re-derives none of this.
how:
Two files, and the split IS the design.

translate.py is PURE — no sockets, no environment, no import of any device. to_provider(messages) turns OpenAI's JSON-STRING tool-call arguments into objects and fills content="" where it is None; both conversions are MEASURED necessities, not anticipated ones (ollama /api/chat refuses the string with "Value looks like object, but can't find closing '}' symbol", measured 2026-09-11 on hex.local against qwen3-coder:30b on the second turn of a tool-using conversation). to_openai(answer) does the return trip: an id ('call_'+uuid4().hex[:20]), type 'function', and arguments re-stringified. completion(answer, model, usage) assembles the chat.completion envelope.

serve.py holds the HTTP handler and takes `resolve` and `models` as CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENTS. It never reaches for inference_domain and cannot be made to — the only way to get an answer out of it is to hand it one. POST /v1/chat/completions and GET /v1/models are the two routes; everything else is a named 404. stream=true is REFUSED BY NAME with the reason on the wire rather than faked. A resolver that raises becomes a named 5xx carrying the exception type, never a 200 with an empty choice. The handler class and make_server() are separate, so the teeth construct a handler with fakes and never open a port.

AND A SECOND PIECE THE CAST FOUND NECESSARY: a machine_imports_no_device sieve in build_inspector, beside device_isolation_holds (inspector.py:3210), discovering machine dirs the way that one discovers device dirs. Measured at cast: the existing sieve returns [] unless row['dir'] starts with 'devices/', so nothing today stops a file under cairn/machines/ from importing cairn.devices.anything. Without this the machine's one load-bearing property is a prose promise.

SOURCE: CairnCommons/measurements/2026-09-11-hermes-openai-door-spike.py (191 lines), which already served a real hermes-agent 0.21.1 and proved each translation on the wire. The build's work is removing its two device imports and its module-level ENDPOINT/MODEL globals — those belong to the holder.
falsifier: DONE when (a) openai_wire imports no device — the new machine_imports_no_device sieve says so, not a reading; (b) translate.py's functions are pure and provable with no network and no fixtures beyond dicts, in BOTH directions (string->object on the way in, object->string on the way out, null content->""); (c) serve.py answers /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models from injected callables alone, and a handler constructed with a resolve that raises returns a named 5xx rather than a coherent empty answer; (d) stream=true is refused with the reason on the wire; and (e) a holder includes it with an injected 'ask inference_domain over the bus' resolve and serves a real tool-using turn end to end. WRONG INTENT if the machine ends up knowing about inference_domain, the bus, or hermes — any of the three means it is a device wearing a machine's name, and the next holder cannot include it. The clauses are lettered so proof_coverage.clauses() demands a tooth per clause instead of falling back to [WHOLE].
traces_to: Law 6 (the sole path to the inference host); Law 1 (the next OpenAI-shaped process re-derives none of this); Law 4 (clause (a) is held by a sieve, not by this paragraph); Akien's rulings of 2026-09-11 on shims owning the outside world and on the machine rung.

watchme.trigger: every component directory in class-space whose source imports cairn.machines.openai_wire — counted from the import graph the sieve already builds, so the probe costs one walk and no new instrument. It fires on the COUNT of distinct holders.
watchme.enough: TWO distinct holders have included it. ONE holder forever is the FINDING, not a pass: the generality was paid for and never collected, and the honest disposition would have been to build the translation inside hermes_shim. The watch does NOT clear on a timer.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, naming the holders found and the import path that made each one count.
watchme.nexus: the decompose tree — when 'build it as its own machine' pays and when it is speculative generality is a split-shaped judgement.
watchme.consumer: Akien, and CC at the next machine-vs-holder fork

gates_bound: proof gate — cairn/machines/openai_wire/proofs/ runs green under the tester at isolation=netns, teeth a hollow build could not pass.
import gate — machine_imports_no_device in build_inspector reds any file under cairn/machines/ importing cairn.devices.*; openai_wire is its first subject.
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage.
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.
children: none, because the two files are one seam over one measured wire format and the sieve is a short sibling of an existing one. The HTTP-listener ownership question that would have been a child was closed by ruling 2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports before cast.
depends_on: none. 548dd13fb4db (PROVED 2026-09-11) already made the one inference door carry a tool-using conversation over the bus verb, which is what an injected resolve will call. cb97524c0e8e (hermes_shim) is this ticket's DEPENDENT and is what answers clause (e).

cast_checks.assumption_check: THREE, named rather than resolved. (1) That an OpenAI-shaped client accepts a plain HTTP base_url with no TLS and no API key — MEASURED TRUE for hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11 and unmeasured for anything else; a client demanding TLS is the meeting shim's finding, not this machine's defect. (2) That non-streaming answers suffice — UNMEASURED, and paid for structurally: stream=true is refused BY NAME on the wire, so the assumption fails loudly the first time it is false instead of degrading into a hang. (3) That 'machine' is the right rung — a machine is tools plus glue and has no process of its own, which is exactly what this is: the process belongs to whichever shim includes it. Akien named the rung himself ('if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it'), so this assumption has his word behind it, not mine.
cast_checks.missing_check: ONE POINT WAS NOT WRAPPED AND IS NOW. The falsifier's clause (a) — 'openai_wire imports no device' — had NO PHYSICS behind it. Measured during this cast: build_inspector's device_isolation_holds (inspector.py:3210) returns [] unless row['dir'] starts with 'devices/', so a file under cairn/machines/ importing cairn.devices.anything is caught by NOTHING today. That makes the machine's one load-bearing property a prose promise, which is the shape Law 4 calls an IOU. So the build carries a second piece: a machine_imports_no_device sieve beside its sibling, discovering machine dirs the way the existing one discovers device dirs. Without it this ticket ships a machine that is a device wearing a machine's name the first time somebody is in a hurry.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: Stated in the ticket, five lettered clauses (a)-(e) so proof_coverage.clauses() demands a tooth per clause rather than falling back to [WHOLE] — a lesson taken from the sibling voyage 548dd13fb4db, where an unlettered five-clause falsifier would have been satisfied by one tooth. HORIZON: (a)-(d) are answerable the moment the machine exists and are the PROVEME bar; (e) — a real holder serving a real tool-using turn — is answered by cb97524c0e8e, which is why that ticket is this one's dependent rather than this one waiting on it. WRONG INTENT is the machine acquiring knowledge of inference_domain, the bus, or hermes.
cast_checks.collision_check: TWO CHECKED, NEITHER TERMINAL. (1) The one-web-server rule — 'a device gets a declared PANE, never its own server'. Its WHY is that the UI must not fragment into per-device servers a human has to remember the ports of; this port serves a machine-to-machine wire format with no UI at all, and ruling 2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports settles it explicitly. A DISTINCTION TO RECORD, not a collision. (2) no-cross-device-imports (ruling 2026-08-31). Its WHY is that a device reaching into another device's internals bypasses the owner's gate; this machine imports NO device at all, which is strictly stronger. Also not a collision — and the check surfaced the missing_check finding above, because asking 'what enforces this?' is what revealed that nothing does.
cast_checks.builder_check: Wearing the cheapest-builder hat, FOUR questions the ticket must answer and now does. (1) 'What exactly is injected, and with what signature?' — resolve(request: dict) -> dict returning inference_domain's own resolve shape ({'answer': {...}, 'hit': bool, 'canonical': str}); models() -> iterable of model names. Both are constructor arguments, and the ticket spells the contract so the builder does not infer it from the spike's closure. (2) 'Where does the endpoint/model/temperature live?' — NOT HERE. The spike has module-level ENDPOINT/MODEL globals reading os.environ; those are the HOLDER'S, and their removal is named build work rather than left for the builder to notice. (3) 'How is a resolver failure answered?' — a named 5xx carrying the exception type, never a 200 with an empty choice; that is clause (c) and it has its own tooth. (4) 'Does serve.py bind a socket at import time?' — no; the handler class and a make_server(...) helper are separate, so the pure teeth can construct a handler with fakes and never open a port.

measured_at_cast.the_physics_hole: build_inspector's device_isolation_holds (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py:3210) opens with `if not row['dir'].startswith('devices/'): return []`, so a file under cairn/machines/ importing cairn.devices.* is caught by nothing. Read directly from the source during the collision_check. The machine rung's meaning has been unenforced for as long as there have been machines; openai_wire is the first component whose value depends on it.
measured_at_cast.the_wire_shape: Taken off a real hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11, not from the schema in my head. The JSON-STRING arguments and the null content were both MEASURED refusals from ollama, and the evidence stays at CairnCommons/measurements/2026-09-11-hermes-openai-door-spike.py.
measured_at_cast.the_model_caveat_carried_forward: qwen3-coder:30b — the only model the shipped stack declares for chat — emits tool calls as TEXT on hex.local ollama 0.30.11, while qwen2.5:7b, llama3.2:3b and devstral-small-2:24b return them structured. That is a MODEL choice belonging to cb97524c0e8e, not a wire-format defect: this machine translates whatever the resolver returns.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Three looked at. (a) Put the port on inference_domain — SPECIFICALLY RULED OUT by Akien on 2026-09-11: 'not an openrouter port on the inference proxy. the shims handle all the interfacing with the outside world.' (b) Put the translation inside hermes_shim — simpler today and wrong tomorrow: the next OpenAI-shaped process (aider, any IDE assistant) would copy it, which is the stone-1 parallel-build failure. Akien closed this one himself: 'if you build it as it's own machine, then anybody can include it.' (c) Use an off-the-shelf proxy (litellm, openai-compatible shims) — it would dial the provider itself, which is the second door Law 6 exists to close, and it would not ride the bus.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That an OpenAI-shaped client will accept a base_url pointing at a plain HTTP port with no TLS and no key. MEASURED TRUE for hermes-agent 0.21.1 on 2026-09-11 (the spike served it), and NOT assumed for any other client — a client that demands TLS is a finding for the shim that meets it, not a defect here. A second assumption, stated because it is load-bearing and unmeasured: that a non-streaming answer is acceptable to the clients that will use this. stream=true is refused by name precisely so that assumption fails loudly instead of quietly.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: Consulted: the compiled intentions model (97 files, recompiled this act) has zero hits for openai, chat completion, or wire format; the ticket corpus has three hits and all three are this conversation's own siblings (548dd13fb4db, cb97524c0e8e, 328d61ee5101). In-house the nearest thing is cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py, which speaks ollama's /api/chat — the OTHER side of this translation, and the reason the machine is needed rather than a reason it is not. Outside: the OpenAI chat-completions schema is the prior art, and it is being IMPLEMENTED here, not reinvented — the shape came off the wire from a real hermes-agent 0.21.1, not from memory.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: Checked against the one-web-server rule (a device gets a declared PANE, never its own server) and it is NOT a collision — ruling 2026-09-11-the-one-web-server-rule-governs-the-ui-not-service-ports settles that the rule governs the UI surface, not service ports, and this port serves a machine-to-machine wire format with no UI. Checked against 'no cross-device imports': this machine imports NO device at all, which is stronger than the rule requires and is clause (a) of its own falsifier.
